prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-29. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.28 |
| Retained earnings       | 302,526M |
| Current liabilities     | 136,661M |
| Current assets          | 175,329M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 414,367M |
| Total liabilities       | 279,861M |
| Total assets            | 694,228M |
| EBIT / operating income | 38,398M |
| Revenue                 | 82,886M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided metrics indicate a very strong balance sheet, with modest leverage (total liabilities/total assets of ~40%), adequate liquidity (current ratio of 1.28), and substantial cumulative profitability (retained earnings of ~44% of total assets). The EBIT margin of ~46% further signals robust cash-flow generation capacity, consistent with an upper-tier investment-grade profile, though the absence of interest-coverage or maturity data prevents an AAA assignment.
DECISION: AA
(The rating uses pre-2026 benchmarks for large-cap industrials/tech with comparable capitalization and margins.)
